section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the findings from Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, which investigated the relationship between cognitive control, divergent thinking, and creative achievement. Both experiments demonstrated that higher divergent thinking scores are associated with greater attentional flexibility and increased cognitive control during attentional switches. However, Experiment 2 specifically found no association between real-life creativity (assessed by ATTA or CAQ) and attentional flexibility or cognitive control, nor between general intelligence (assessed by WASI) and creativity (CAQ/ATTA). Figure 8 illustrates a correlation from Experiment 2.
